answers.explanation: SCPs apply to all principals in member accounts — even AdministratorAccess cannot override an explicit SCP Deny. Night 1 miss.
RAM shares subnets, TGW attachments, and other resources across accounts. Identity Center is workforce SSO, not resource sharing. Night 1 miss.
Fargate pulls images and writes logs via the task execution role. The task role is for application AWS API calls at runtime. Night 6 Q4 miss.
Cross-account KMS requires both key policy trust on the CMK and IAM permissions on the caller. Night 2 miss.
S3 Bucket Key reduces KMS API calls for SSE-KMS. Transfer Acceleration speeds uploads — it does not reduce KMS charges. Night 6 Q7 miss.
Secrets Manager stores secret values with optional automatic rotation. KMS stores encryption keys, not application passwords. Nights 2–3 miss.
Bucket policy Deny on PutObject without SSE-KMS enforces encryption at upload. Night 2 Q9 miss.
CloudFront WAF Web ACLs use CLOUDFRONT scope and are created in us-east-1. Night 4 miss.
ALB WAF uses REGIONAL scope in the same Region as the load balancer. Night 4 Q4 miss.
Firewall Manager deploys WAF (and other) policies org-wide from a central admin account. Night 4/6 miss.
Log file validation creates SHA-256 digest files for tamper detection. Data events log S3/Lambda API activity — different purpose. Night 5 Q4 miss.
Config rules evaluate current resource configuration state continuously. CloudWatch alarms on metrics, not compliance state. Night 6 Q17 miss.
Security Hub = findings dashboard. Firewall Manager = policy deployment (WAF, SG, etc.). Night 6 Q14 miss.
Access Analyzer evaluates resource policies for external/cross-account access paths. Control Tower = landing zone. Night 6 Q19 miss.
Control Tower provides multi-account landing zone with guardrails and Account Factory. Access Analyzer finds external access, not account vending.
